project: prompt-miner score clamp censors the statistic the marker gate reads
description: rev 2, revised against 15 findings from two adversarial critics (2 high, 7 medium, 6 low; see critique.md). scoreSession at .oh/skills/prompt-miner/scripts/mine-traces.mjs:427 computes clamp(base + bonus, 0, 100). base is already capped at 100 by construction and bonus adds up to 15, so every low-friction ground-truth session lands on the ceiling: 15 of 37 other-stratum sessions (41%) sit at exactly 100 on the 2026-08-13 run. The marker gate (references/markers.md:55-58) promotes on a standardized mean difference in that censored score. Measured: lenWords>=25 in stratum other is d=0.332 capped with 19/37 leave-one-out folds under the bar, and d=0.423 uncensored with 0/37 folds under the bar - the clamp, not the data, decides the robustness verdict. Fix: emit scoreUncapped = base + bonus as an additive sibling of score (score itself unchanged, still clamped), add a per-stratum manifest.ceilingSaturation census computed over rankable with atCeiling counting stored rounded score === 100, name scoreUncapped as the correlation scale in markers.md AND in SKILL.md (the doc an agent actually executes), and add a stability guard: the marker record carries effect_size (uncensored, authoritative) alongside effect_size_capped, and a marker whose two scales disagree on sign or on bar-clearing is reported UNSTABLE and is not promotable on either scale. The guard is what keeps the net change stricter rather than looser: it would have blocked the 2026-08-09 referencesSkill promotion that #730 already identified as a clamp artifact. Explicitly does NOT close #730 (cross-window irreproducibility); no window, threshold, or cross-run rule is touched.

userStories.title: The manifest and markdown report carry a per-stratum ceiling-saturation census

acceptanceCriteria: manifest.ceilingSaturation is an object keyed by session type; each value is { atCeiling: <int>, total: <int> }
